title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a handwritten table of contents (8 sections, with page references p.1 to p.29) for the manuscript that begins on the next page, 'Rétrospection sur les cartes (finies)'. That manuscript is Grothendieck's systematic reworking of the theory of finite (topological, cellular) maps, i.e. dessins d'enfants, around 1981-82, contemporaneous with the Esquisse d'un programme. The sections are as follows.

(1) The combinatorial description of maps via the cartographic group and its index-2 'oriented' subgroup. Read from the next page:
- C_2 = Γ_2 = <τ_0, τ_1, τ_2 | τ_i^2 = (τ_0τ_2)^2 = 1>.
- Γ_2^0 = ker(Γ_2 → Z/2) = <ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ | ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0 = ρ_1^2 = 1>.
- There is an equivalence between the isotopy category of finite maps and finite 'special' Γ_2-sets.

(2) Weighted triangular maps and the groups π_{0,3} and π_{0,3}^τ. Here π_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. The τ-version is presumably the extension by complex conjugation (an orientation-reversing involution), matching the non-orientable maps allowed in (1).

(3) The relation with finite coverings of U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} and with algebraic curves. This is the Belyi / dessins correspondence.

(4) Imposing ρ_i^{ν_i} = 1 and fundamental groups 'à signature'. These are orbifold fundamental groups, i.e. triangle groups Δ(ν_0, ν_1, ν_∞), and their quotients classify maps whose vertex, edge and face valencies divide the ν_i.

(5) On the existence of a weighting (pondération) of a given triangular map. That is: when can valency data be assigned so that the map comes from an orbifold covering?

(6) The map associated to a convex polygon, and the associated fundamental groups.

(7) The relation to weighted n-polygonal maps. This presumably generalises from triangles to n-gons, i.e. from π_{0,3} towards π_{0,n} and polygon groups.

(8) Introduction of an object read as PΣ^×_{p_n} (uncertain) and of the fundamental 2-groupoid. This links to the previous page, which defines the semidirect-product (action) groupoid Π_1(X,G) for a group G acting on a space X, with composition (ℓ',g')(ℓ,g) = (ℓ'∘g'(ℓ), g'g). This is the standard device for an orbifold/stack fundamental groupoid, and it seems the plan was to upgrade it to a 2-groupoid.

The page as a whole maps the route Grothendieck took: combinatorial maps → Belyi coverings → orbifold (triangle) groups → polygonal generalisation → higher-groupoid formulation.
errors: No mathematical claims are made on this page, so there is nothing to check. The page references with primes (5', 9', 12') indicate reinserted or renumbered sheets.

missed.claim: There is a dedicated section on when a triangular map admits a weighting, i.e. a compatible orbifold signature. This question is not treated as such in Esquisse. Its content cannot be judged from the table of contents alone.
missed.quote: Sur l'existence d'une pondération d'une carte triangulaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may contain criteria relating combinatorial triangulations to orbifold uniformisation. The relevant pages 12'-15 would need checking.

missed.claim: The plan passes from triangular maps to maps attached to convex polygons and n-polygonal weighted maps, ending with a fundamental 2-groupoid. This is a combinatorial route from π_{0,3} to π_{0,n} and higher groupoids that is not spelled out in published form.
missed.quote: Relation aux cartes n-polygonales pondérées ... Introduction de PΣ^×_{p_n} et du 2-groupoïde fondamental
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is potentially relevant to combinatorial models of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower (M_{0,n}) and to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme. Its novelty depends on the content of pp. 15-29.

deep.surprise_reason: This is only a table of contents. Its topics largely match the Esquisse (cartographic groups, Belyi, triangle groups, Teichmüller groupoids). Only sections 5-8 hint at possibly unpublished details, which this page alone does not reveal.
transcription_corrections: Item 1: '𝔖_2 et 𝔖_2^0' should be the cartographic group and its oriented subgroup, written C_2 / Γ_2 and C_2^0 / Γ_2^0 (as on the next page), not symmetric groups.
Item 2: the groups read as π_{0,3} and a τ-variant (π_{0,3}^τ, probably π_{0,3} extended by the conjugation τ); the reading of the superscript remains uncertain.
Item 8: the symbol read 'PΣ^×_{p_n}' is uncertain.
